saints.name: St. Waltrude
saints.title: Abbess
saints.shortBlurb: A noblewoman of Hainaut whose convent became the seed of the city of Mons…
biography: Born at Cousolre in Hainaut, daughter of the nobles Walbert and Bertilia and sister of Aldegonde, foundress of Maubeuge, Waltrude married Vincent Madelgarus, count of Hainaut, and bore him four children — Landry, Dentelin, Aldetrude, and Madelberta — who with their parents were all venerated as saints.

About 656, after young Dentelin's death, the couple resolved to part: Vincent became a monk in the monastery he had founded at Hautmont. Waltrude gave herself to prayer and almsdeeds, ransoming captives at her own cost, and gathered a company of virgins at Castrilocus — Châteaulieu, the 'castle place' — the hill around which the city of Mons grew up.

She died on 9 April about the year 688. Her relics rest in the collegiate church of Sainte-Waudru at Mons, and each year the city draws her shrine through its streets on a gilded cart, the car d'or, in the festival called the Ducasse. Because the town grew from her convent, she is honored as mother and patroness of Mons.
saints.knownFor: Founding the community that grew into the city of Mons.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 9 April
